text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As Suncorp chairman Graham Tucker claimed the Queensland Government's proposed A$19 billion mega-bank merger was not in the interests of Suncorp and the State, the plan has been dealt a serious blow with the shock resignation yesterday of Tucker and two other directors of the giant Suncorp insurance and building society group - Ted Ranson and John Wruck. Page 1.

Frank Lowy, who controls Westfield Corp, and Dick Pratt, both of whom are well known for their political connections in Australia, have emerged as sizeable donors to the 1996 US presidential campaign - Lowy is backing President Clinton, while Pratt's Pratt Industries is backing both parties. Page 1.

Ansett Australia AIRa.NZ, which began operating in Taiwan in November, has issued free tickets worth at least A$300,000 in order to avoid passengers staging aircraft "sit-ins" in protest at delays or late arrivals. Taiwan had 26 such "piracies" last year and has seen an increasing number of incidents this year. Page 1.

Following a decision by Japanese electronics giant NEC to make its local subsidiary a mobile telephone engine room, digital mobile phones designed and manufactured in this country will soon hit the world market. The move is expected to create export revenue of more than A$35 million this financial year from offshore sales. Page 3.

Poker machine giant Aristocrat Leisure Ltd managing director Gary Garton told The Australian Financial Review yesterday the group is moving to exploit the market for in-flight and hotel room gambling as rapid changes in technology in the poker-machine industry would see the games increasingly available outside pubs and clubs. Page 19.

Mobile phone company Mobile Communications Holdings Ltd has sold a group of non-core assets, including cellular phone retailer Mobiletronics and a 10 per cent stake in billing company United Telecommunications, for a profit of more than 300 per cent. Managing director and majority shareholder Philip Cornish said the company would end up with about A$17 million extra cash after the initial transactions. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Daniel Petre, Microsoft's man in Australia and the man regarded as the leader of this country's computer 'brat pack', has shocked the multimedia industry by quitting his position as director of Microsoft's Advanced Technology Group - a position specially created for him several years ago - to live a more relaxed lifestyle and spend more time with his family. Page 3.

The Queensland Government's A$19 billion megabank merger was dealt a humiliating blow yesterday when three directors of Suncorp Insurance and Finance, including Suncorp deputy chairman Ted Ranson and director John Wruck, shocked a Brisbane function to unveil Suncorp's A$202.6 million June year profit by announcing their resignations. Page 19.

Coles Myer Ltd, which now runs Australia's biggest electronic funds at point of sale (EFTPOS) network, has signalled an upcoming battle between banks and retailers with a submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system which calls for the dumping of special status for banks inside the payments system, which facilitates the flow of cash in this country. Page 19.

In a move which is the latest in a series of expansionary moves by Ireland-based Independent Newspapers Plc - controlled by the O'Reilly family - into Australia and New Zealand, INP yesterday launched a full cash or scrip takeover bid for New Zealand's largest publisher, Wilson & Horton. Page 19.

Peter Hammond, the managing director of local manufacturer and distributor of paper-based stationery products Spicers Paper, has revealed the company will be merging its separate operations, Spicers Stationery and Croxley Collins Olympic, in a move which he says recognises the reality of stiff import competition and spritely new entrants. Page 21.

Adelaide-based alcoholic lemonade drink maker Two Dogs has signed a 15-year deal with UK drinks giant HP Bulmer, believed to be worth A$150 million based on the expected increase in annual sales in Australasia, to manufacture and market the company's products in Australia and New Zealand. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After announcing a 99 per cent increase in annual profit to A$201 million yesterday, three Suncorp board members, including chairman Graham Tucker, resigned in protest at the lack of information they had recieved form the Queensland Government on the mergr that will see Suncorp, Metway Bank and Queensland Industry Development Corp form the fifth largest banking group in Australia. Page 27.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels yesterday conceded that although there was insufficient evidence to take action against Santos' purchase of the Australian oil and gas assets of US group Parker and Parsley, the ACCC is still concerned about the increase in concentration caused by the acquisition. Page 29.

Vodafone shareholder Mobile Communications Holdings has scored a profit of A$12.5 million from the sale of its wholly owned subsidiary Mobiletronics Communications, its 24.9 per cent shareholding in service provider Martin Dawes Australia and part of its shareholding in billing company United International Telecommunications. Page 29.

The Investment Funds Association yesterday launched a A$1 million campaign to encourage the market to abandon terms such as "unit trusts" and "managed funds" in favour of the banner "managed investments" and to promote the funds as a way into the range of asset classes rather than as a separate asset class. Page 29.

According to the Reserve Bank's study, The Future of the Financial System, the exponential growth in derivatives will force changes in bank supervision. The Bank's deputy governor Graeme Thompson said rule-based approaches to supervision are likely to beome less effective because they fail to seize the rapidly-changing risk associated with financial and derivative markets. Page 29.

The New South Wales Court of Appeal yesterday dismissed a summary judgment obtained two years ago by ANZ Banking which enabled it to seize properties worth A$6.7 million from Trawl Industries of Australia Pty Ltd, claiming that the company was heavily in debt. Page 29.
THE AGE

Dr Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers is bidding NZ$10.50 a share for the 44.88 per cent of newspaper publisher Wilson and Horton it does not already own, in a bid to become New Zealand's largest media owner. The offer values the country's flagship newspaper publisher at NZ$1.03 billion. Page C1.

Although still highly concerned that the move would hinder the creation of a competitive market for natural gas, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission yesterday ended a five-month long investigation into Santos' purchase of the Australian assts of American oil group Parker and Parsley, claiming there was not enough evidence to take the matter further. Page C1.

Unconvinced that the Queensland Government's planned A$19 billion mega-merger is in the best interests of Suncorp, three board members, including chairman Graham Tucker, stepped down from Suncorp yesterday. The board members complained of a lack of information on the merger, under which insurance and investment group Suncorp, Metway Bank and Queensland Industry Development Corp will join forces. Page C3.

Carlton and United Breweries head Nuno D'Aquino last week announced details of a plan to ensure the brewer is positioned for growth into the next century, after achieving double-digit profit growth over each of the past three years. CUB made a 13 per cent increase in operating profit to A$327 million in the year to June 30. Page C3.

Spicers Paper yesterday announced the merging of two of its stationery operations to be completed by April next year, creating Spicer and Collins Stationery, which Spicers expects to have an annual turnover of about A$200 million. Page C3.

Earnings of Australia's major sharemarket-listed companies could fall because of a new accounting standard on the rate at which they depreciate assets this financial year. Telstra and Amcor reviewed their depreciation rates a year early and booked windfall profits for the 1996 financial year. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
